step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram and transcript present Macquarie Bank's DEFT serverless edge security architecture. Requests originate from the client browser/mobile application (DEFT.COM.AU) and enter AWS through AWS Shield for DDoS protection. Traffic passes through AWS WAF for web application security filtering and reaches Amazon CloudFront CDN at edge locations. CloudFront invokes Lambda@Edge to perform security controls (HSTS injection, X-Frame-Options, JWT token authentication). Static single-page application assets are fetched from Amazon S3 in the AWS Region and delivered back to the client via CloudFront.

graph.name: Macquarie Bank Deft Serverless Payment Architecture
graph.notes: Serverless edge architecture replacing 60 EC2 instances to secure payment web applications with PCI DSS Level 1 compliance.

nodes.name: DEFT.COM.AU
nodes.notes: Client web browser or mobile application accessing DEFT payment platform.

nodes.name: Shield
nodes.notes: Provides DDoS protection at the AWS Edge.

nodes.name: WAF
nodes.notes: Applies application-specific security controls to filter malicious traffic.

nodes.name: CloudFront
nodes.notes: Content delivery network caching S3 application content at edge locations.

nodes.name: Lambda@Edge
nodes.notes: Performs security header injection (HSTS, X-Frame-Options) and JWT token validation.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Stores single-page application (SPA) static assets in the AWS Region.

edges.notes: Client sends HTTP/HTTPS request to DEFT application via Shield.
DDoS-protected traffic passed to AWS WAF.
Filtered web traffic passed to CloudFront edge distribution.
CloudFront triggers Lambda@Edge for security and authorization checks.
Lambda@Edge and CloudFront request origin assets from S3 in the AWS Region.
CloudFront returns secure, cached static assets back to DEFT client.
